lead: Amarillo plumbing deals with hard water, wind, sudden cold fronts and clay soil. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across Amarillo.
risk: hard water scale, frozen pipes in cold snaps and slab leaks
risk_short: hard water, frozen pipes and slab leaks
why: Wolflin, Olsen Park and the San Jacinto area have homes from the 1920s to the 1950s with galvanized supply lines and cast-iron drains. Newer areas in the southwest sit on slabs.
Blue northers drop temperatures fast and strong wind pulls heat from walls and attics, so pipes freeze quickly. Expansive soils stress slab plumbing.
water: Amarillo draws on groundwater from the Ogallala and other aquifers plus water from the Canadian River Municipal Water Authority. It is hard.
tips: Insulate attic and wall pipes before winter.
Disconnect hoses when a cold front is coming.
Watch your water bill for slab leak signs.
areas: PipeMend works in Wolflin, Olsen Park, Bivins, the San Jacinto area, Puckett, the Colonies, Downtown and every other Amarillo neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits come from the City of Amarillo Building Safety Department, and plumbers must hold a Texas license.

faq.q: Why do Amarillo pipes freeze so fast?
faq.a: Cold fronts can drop the temperature sharply in hours, and Panhandle wind pulls heat out of walls and attics. Pipes there freeze first. Insulation and dripping faucets help.
